Notes: c. 46-47 CE (start of Paul's first missionary journey, conventionally dated c. 46-48 CE). Acts 13:5: on arriving at Salamis, Barnabas and Saul 'proclaimed the word of God in the Jewish synagogues' (plural). Earliest Salamis-specific documented Jewish presence and basis for Year Established. Scale: an organized community with more than one synagogue; M. N. Tod (ISBE 'Salamis', biblehub.com/atlas/salamis.htm) reads the plural as 'pointing to the existence of several synagogues and thus of a large Jewish community in Salamis'. No numerical estimate for the Jews of Salamis was found. Context not entered as rows because it concerns Cyprus as a whole, not Salamis: Roman circular of c. 139 BCE sent also to Cyprus (1 Macc 15:23); Josephus Ant. 13.284-287 (c. 105-100 BCE) on the flourishing Jews of Cyprus; Philo Legatio 282 lists Cyprus among islands full of Jewish colonies; Herod's lease of half the Cypriot copper mines (12 BCE); Jewish coins well attested on the island from the late 2nd c. BCE to c. 70 CE (Destrooper-Georgiades 2006). The Tyndale Bible Dictionary claim that the Ptolemies encouraged Jews to settle at Salamis is undated and unsupported by cited evidence, and the tradition that Barnabas (a Cypriot Levite, Acts 4:36) came from Salamis is legend, so neither is counted. Later (outside period): in the revolt of 116-117 CE under Artemion the Jews of Cyprus reportedly sacked Salamis; Cassius Dio 68.32 gives 240000 dead (gentile victims, island-wide, an ancient figure) and says Jews were then barred from Cyprus.
